recommendation: Keep the no-change audit. No core source follow-up is needed unless OO makes a new decision to add a specific modern blood-product, fetus, or donor example to Observation.focus/code guidance.
issue_request: FHIR-7157 was a Published/Persuasive OO clarification from the 2015 May DSTU1 ballot asking to add Observation.subject comment text that the distinction between a patient's own observation value and that of a fetus, donor, blood product unit, etc. is often specified in Observation.code.
initial_application: Git commit 89739dcf150cb051d4f4a26d48e1a827649c9af5 historically applied #7152, #7155, and #7157 by appending the requested sentence to the old Observation.subject spreadsheet comment. Later commit 8da41eb1e5b69c9ac8d6b759ba1c88e9d892b881 removed that exact DSTU1 comment wording while replacing it with the modern subject/focus/code model.
additional_context: Later final OO decisions changed the modeling surface. FHIR-14443 promoted focal-subject semantics into Observation.focus, FHIR-43357 approved current focus wording and examples, and sibling issue FHIR-7156 is already represented on the combined branch by a no-change audit. On the latest combined branch, Observation is in the active build, Observation.subject says `focus` or `code` itself specifies the actual focus when it differs from the subject, and the Observation notes say the distinction between the subject and what is directly measured is specified in Observation.code itself.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current build-scope StructureDefinition and notes preserve the implementer-relevant rule from FHIR-7157 without the obsolete DSTU1 indirect-target example sentence.
